meta.title: {name} – collect KPIs from all your sites, with the evidence
meta.description: Free software to collect KPIs from across your organisation, with the evidence behind each figure. Totals are calculated at every level, templates for the voluntary standard VS and the revised ESRS are included, and the auditor checks everything in the tool.

hero.title: Collect KPIs from all your sites, with the evidence attached
hero.lead: Contributors enter their figures and attach the supporting file. {name} adds everything up across your organisation and keeps it ready for the auditor. It's free software, and you set it up yourself.
proofs: A read-only auditor role: values, evidence, and history
The voluntary standard VS, with an export to EFRAG's official workbook
On your server, or managed hosting with Clever Cloud

features.title: Run the whole collection in one place
features.lead: You open a campaign for the year or the quarter. Each contributor sees what they still have to fill in, and reminders go out automatically.
points: The figure from the comparison period (N-1) appears next to the field, with the variance.
Numbers, percentages, amounts, yes / no, choice lists, written text, and tables with a variable number of rows.
A site that opens during the year counts from its opening date.
You see the completion rate of each organisation live.

features.title: The evidence sits next to each figure
features.lead: Each value keeps its file and its history: who entered it, who validated it, and when.
points: The auditor gets read-only access and checks everything in the tool.
A closed year stays as it was published: the organisation tree and the figures of the time are kept.
No more digging through emails for invoices the day before the audit.

features.title: Group totals are calculated for you
features.lead: You set up your organisation with your own levels. A figure entered for a site is counted in every total above it.
points: Your own levels and names, as many as you need.
You write the formulas yourself, in the tool. You don't need a developer.
Dashboards and charts, including comparisons with previous periods.

features.title: Strange values show up before the audit
features.lead: The tool compares each value with the comparison period and with your own rules. Anything that needs a look goes into one list, To be handled.
points: Each alert explains the problem in one sentence.
The contributor either fixes the value or explains why it's right.

features.title: Start from a template
features.lead: The library has fourteen templates: the European voluntary standard for sustainability reporting (VS), as two templates, Basic and Comprehensive; pay transparency; and the revised ESRS of the CSRD, as eleven templates, one for each standard. You can change any KPI, unit, or formula afterwards.
points: A setup wizard walks you through it, from your organisation to your first campaign.
You can import values from Excel or CSV, and export tables that open cleanly in Excel.
It helps you collect the data you need for the voluntary standard VS, for your ESRS metrics, and for gender pay gap reporting under the EU directive 2023/970.
For the ESRS, install ESRS 2 and the templates of your material topics. A KPI that two templates share is entered once.

features.title: Simple for people who sign in only twice a year
features.lead: The data entry page tells them in one sentence what's left to do. It works on a phone, in seven languages.
points: Statuses use a symbol and a word, not just a colour.
You can translate your KPIs with an Excel file.
A short guide for each role opens from the help icon, in the language of the interface.

items.a: Yes. There's no paid version, and the source code is public under the AGPL-3.0-or-later licence. The only cost is hosting.
You can try it on your computer, install it on a server with Docker, or use managed hosting with Clever Cloud. The Get {name} page gives the commands and the links.
Wherever you choose: on one of your company's servers, installed by your IT team, or with a hosting service that runs it for you (Clever Cloud). Backups run automatically.

items.q: Do we have to give up Excel?
items.a: No. You can import values from Excel or CSV files, and export tables back to Excel.

items.q: Does {name} support the voluntary standard VS?
items.a: Yes. The library has it as a Basic and a Comprehensive template. {name} helps you collect the data you need for it, and exports the values to EFRAG's official workbook.

Yes. The library has a template for gender pay gap reporting under the EU directive 2023/970, with one report per employer. Each entity enters its average pay and headcounts, and {name} calculates the mean gaps of each entity and of the group from the totals, never as an average of gaps. National laws that transpose the directive can add details: the template follows the directive.

items.q: Does {name} have templates for the ESRS?
items.a: Yes. The library has eleven templates for the revised ESRS of the CSRD (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1563): ESRS 2, E1 to E5, S1 to S4, and G1. They are collection templates built from the text of the regulation. Install ESRS 2 and the templates of your material topics, then adapt the KPIs to your company. A KPI that several templates share is entered once. The KPI texts of these templates are in English and French.

items.q: Does {name} make us compliant with a regulation?
items.a: No, not by itself. It helps you collect the quantitative data you need, for example for the voluntary standard VS, for your ESRS metrics, or for gender pay gap reporting.
No. It collects the data and applies the formulas you set. It is not certified carbon accounting software.
No. The data entry page tells them what's left to do, on a computer or a phone.
Each value with its evidence and its history. They can't change anything.

items.q: What happens to a closed year?
items.a: It stays as it was published, with the organisation tree and the figures of the time. If an administrator reopens it, they choose whether to keep those figures or to recalculate with today's organisation.
Yes. You can create separate spaces in one installation, for example for ESG, purchasing, and HR.
Yes, if an administrator allows it. It is off by default. Each person connects their own assistant, with a personal token, and the assistant has that person's rights, never more.

items.q: What does IT need to do?
items.a: Host it and apply the updates. There's nothing to develop.

own: Create your KPIs one by one in the tool, with their units and formulas.
Reuse KPIs you already have in other frameworks: a shared figure is entered once.
Import an Excel or JSON file. You see a preview before anything changes.

vs.title: The voluntary standard VS, ready to collect
vs.lead: {name} helps you collect the data you need for the voluntary standard VS (formerly VSME). Two templates cover it, and you can export the values to EFRAG's official workbook.
points: Every disclosure is a set of KPIs, with its definition, unit, and the evidence behind each value.
Consistency rules catch the usual slips, for example, more renewable electricity than total electricity.
You collect once, site by site, and the values consolidate up the organisation tree.

templates.name: Basic module
templates.text: Disclosures B1 to B11, from the basis for preparation to corruption and bribery.

templates.name: Comprehensive module
templates.text: Disclosures C1 to C9, added to the Basic module: strategy, climate targets and risks, workforce, human rights, gender diversity.

export: Collect and validate the values in {name}.
Export them to EFRAG's official Excel workbook. {name} fills in only the input cells.
Open the workbook in Excel and save it, so that EFRAG's converter can read the calculated values.
